value: Did you mean how many SHOPS have been restructured, or how many TRADING PERIODS ended in a restructuring? — "shops that were rebuilt or replaced, counting a shop once however often it happened" is 6; "tenancies that ended in a restructuring, so a shop restructured twice counts twice" is 7. The entire difference is one shop: Contoso Store New Brunswick (site 7) was restructured twice, closing 2014-03-09 and again 2018-02-02; the other five were restructured once each. WHAT THE CHOICE DOES NOT CHANGE: the shops involved are the same six either way — New Brunswick (CA), South Australia (AU), Mecklenburg-Vorpommern (DE), Delaware, North Dakota and Rhode Island (US). It is unaffected by the physical/online channel (every restructured row is a physical shop; the web shop carries no status), by any date window (none was named, so this covers all time, and nothing is recorded after 2018-02-02), and by open-versus-closed (restructured is a kind of closed, so the 57 trading shops are out under either reading). If you meant "how many restructurings have there been", that is also 7. I cannot pick for you: the Store concept's grounding declares `counts store_key`, which is 7, while dim_store.location_code is declared "what a store is counted by" and dim_location.units_ever_here says "a site re-tenanted twice has three store rows and is one store", which is 6 — and the Store definition itself concedes that "one word came to name two grains".

The 7 rows of contoso_served.dim_store whose status_annotation is exactly 'Restructured', drawn from all 74 rows on record. NO channel predicate: store.resolution.a_version_is_a_row_and_a_row_has_no_channel names "list all restructured stores" as a question about the record and forbids it, and it is immaterial anyway because all 7 Restructured rows are physical and the online sentinel's status is null. NO trading-state predicate: the question names the `restructured` member, declared `of: closed` by store.resolution.active_is_the_absent_close_date, which displaces the `active` default — had that default applied it would have read the 57 rows with no close date and answered 0. NO date window, per order.default.an_unscoped_question_covers_all_time. Over that set the rows returned 6 distinct location_code and 7 distinct store_key (also 7 rows and 6 distinct store_name). I am claiming neither figure as the answer; the two populations those figures count — six places and seven sets of premises — are the choice I am handing back.
